title: Powering Critical Infrastructure
summary: Trace critical power paths and relate load, backup, and capacity without servicing equipment.
objectives: Trace a conceptual utility-to-server power path.
Explain critical load, backup, and capacity in a simulated design.

vocab.def: Equipment or work that needs planned power continuity.
The amount of electrical demand a system can support.
An alternate resource available when the primary resource is interrupted.

sections.heading: Follow the infrastructure
sections.body: A simplified path is utility, facility distribution, UPS, generator, rack power, and server. Real designs include controls, safeguards, and qualified operators.

sections.heading: Load and capacity
sections.body: A critical load needs enough planned capacity. A design team compares demand with available support and considers what happens during an interruption.

sections.heading: Simulation boundary
sections.body: Use a diagram or synthetic power table. Do not service a UPS or generator, open a power supply, access a panel, or perform mains-voltage measurements.

practice.prompt: A simulated rack load rises above its planned capacity. What evidence should a learner record, and what safe escalation should follow?

quiz.question: What is a critical load?
options: Equipment or work needing planned power continuity
